newsitem.title: USA: Oregon's unemployment rate rose in October - report.
newsitem.headline: Oregon's unemployment rate rose in October - report.

text.p: Oregon's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose two tenths of a percentage points to 5.2 percent in October, the state Employment Department said on Tuesday.

October's rise in unemployment correspended with a slowdown in the rate of job growth. For the first nine months of this year, the state's seasonally adjusted nonfarm payroll employment growth averaged 5,000 per month.
The state added 8,000 seasonally adjusted jobs in July, 6,000 in August, 5,800 in September, and 2,400 in October, the Employment Department said.

"For the last three years, we have seen rapid job growth with low levels of unemployment," said David Cooke, an economist with the Employment Department. "Although Oregon's economy is still expanding, several sectors took a breather in October."

The job tallies from the monthly business survey showed seasonally adjusted job declines in nondurable goods manufacturing and services. Most other sectors showed modest job gains. Construction posted a strong gain.
